summary: Mauritius's Passport and Immigration Office lists the nationalities admitted without a visa — including the EU, UK and US — and those that receive a visa on arrival; the passports on its list that need a visa arrange it before travel, and visas are issued free of charge.

travelInsurance.text: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry for ordinary visits. Applicants for the Premium Travel Visa must produce sufficient travel and health insurance for the initial period of stay, the Economic Development Board's Premium Visa page states.

onwardTicket.text: Mauritius's Passport and Immigration Office requires every visitor to hold a valid return ticket to their country of origin or residence.

proofOfFunds.text: Every visitor must have adequate funds to meet the cost of the stay and a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation. The Passport and Immigration Office publishes no daily amount for tourists.

The Passport and Immigration Office cites the Quarantine (Health Declaration Form) Regulations 2026.

declarations.name: Ebola entry restriction and quarantine (DR Congo, Uganda, South Sudan)
declarations.text: Foreign nationals who have travelled from, transited through or been present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days are temporarily barred from entering Mauritius. Mauritian nationals and foreign nationals holding a valid work, residence, occupation, business or student permit may enter but must complete 21 days of mandatory quarantine.

currencyLimits.text: If you carry more than MUR 500,000, you must declare it when you arrive and when you leave, according to Australia's travel advice; this covers all forms of currency, not only cash. The Mauritius Revenue Authority's customs pages set the same Rs 500,000 threshold on arrival (Red Channel) and on departure, for currency, bearer negotiable instruments, precious stones and metals and other high-value goods; departing travellers fill in the Currency Declaration Form at the Customs counter.

notes: The UK government's travel advice says illegal drugs, including cannabis, carry severe penalties, including long jail sentences, and that anyone found with drugs is unlikely to be bailed. Canada's advice adds that some pharmaceutical drugs are prohibited and that owning cigarette papers or rolling machines is illegal.

The Mauritius Revenue Authority says plants and plant products — including fresh fruit and vegetables, seeds and soil — are subject to phytosanitary control and must be declared to Customs; importing animals requires an import permit from the Veterinary Service beforehand.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says most crime is non-violent, such as burglaries from tourist villas and theft of unattended bags, that petty crime is common in tourist areas such as Port Louis, Grand Baie and Flic en Flac, and that there have been some reports of sexual assaults on tourists. It advises not walking alone at night on beaches or in poorly lit areas.

tips.text: The Premium Visa, free of charge, lets foreign nationals stay in Mauritius for one year, renewable, as tourists, retirees or professionals working remotely from Mauritius, with their families. The Passport and Immigration Office links to an online application.

The UK government's travel advice says the tropical cyclone season usually runs from November to May and that Mauritius Meteorological Services issues phased warnings. During a cyclone you are not allowed to leave your accommodation, and car insurance policies often become invalid.
The Passport and Immigration Office requires every visitor to have a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation, adequate funds for the stay and a valid return ticket.

Canada's travel advice says certain coastal waters are prone to riptides. It advises respecting the areas reserved for swimming and warning flags, and asking residents and tour operators about hazards and safe swimming areas.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mauritius?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. The Passport and Immigration Office's 2025 list admits citizens of the EU, UK, US and other listed countries and territories without a visa, gives other nationalities a visa on arrival, and says which passports must arrange a visa before traveling. Visas are issued free of charge.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Mauritius as a tourist?
faq.answer: EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Mauritius visa waiver agreement. The UK, Canadian, Chinese and Russian governments tell their citizens they can stay up to 60 days. The Passport and Immigration Office's country list gives a visa on arrival for sixty days or for two weeks, depending on nationality, and gives no maximum stay for the other visa-free nationalities. The Passport and Immigration Office handles extensions of visa; applicants call in person with documents including bank statements and a confirmed accommodation booking.

faq.question: What is the Mauritius Premium Travel Visa?
faq.answer: A free visa for foreign nationals who want a long stay in Mauritius as a tourist, a retiree or a professional working remotely, with their family. It allows a stay of one year, renewable. The Passport and Immigration Office links to an online application.

faq.question: What do I need to show on arrival in Mauritius?
faq.answer: A passport valid beyond your stay, a valid return ticket to your country of origin or residence, a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation, and adequate funds for the stay (no daily amount is published).

faq.question: When is cyclone season in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The UK and Canadian governments' travel advice says the tropical cyclone season usually runs from November to May. The UK advice says that during a cyclone you are not allowed to leave your accommodation; Canada's advises being ready to change travel plans at short notice in that period.
